title: Simplified colored frontier landscape
prompts:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: a revised, much simpler editorial landscape for the space below the table of contents of No Place To Land.
Input image: the supplied frontier-landscape-v1.png is the concept/composition reference and edit target. Preserve its thesis, but comprehensively transform its rendering and simplify it for small printed placement.
Primary request: replace the intricate blue engraving with an ACTUAL COLORED LANDSCAPE rendered as a beautiful realistic miniature terrain diorama / painterly three-dimensional landscape cutout, on a genuinely TRANSPARENT background. It must sit elegantly on a white page, occupy under half an A4 page, and remain clear at approximately 165 mm wide by 90 mm high. Landscape aspect about 1.8:1.
Keep the two-frontier idea: a small established operating settlement occupies the near-left portion of a larger landscape. Its sustained-use boundary sits well inside the more expansive frontier of technically feasible production. Between them, some possible operating connections are still being constructed and some terrain remains unexplored. Useful applications and the conditions supporting them are not all known in advance. This is not an engineer who fails to understand existing customer value.
Composition: ONE organically shaped, obliquely viewed landscape cutout. Use just three or four broad terrain shapes: a settled low plateau, a simple open valley, and a larger uncharted upland. Established settlement consists of THREE bold, readable building masses, not a city. The gap contains ONE substantial unfinished connecting bridge and ONE simple construction site with a foundation and a crane. A completed route has one short branch suggesting reusable access. The wider uncharted terrain has broad open ground, without a catalogue of ready-made valuable destinations.
Two clear conceptual boundaries: a strong dark blue curved line around the small established-use area and a separate widely spaced dark blue dashed arc farther out across the broader terrain. Keep them visually distinct from the roads and bridge. Their positions should be easily visible at small size. No labels or text baked into the image; labels will be typeset separately.
Style/medium: substantial, realistic landforms with sculptural clarity, restrained natural greens and warm stone colors, muted slate-blue water or accents if needed, soft daylight, strong readable silhouettes and moderate contrast against a white page. A sophisticated editorial landscape, not a diagram made from blue lines and not a toy-world full of tiny details.
Transparency: actual alpha background outside the landscape; no sky, no white rectangle, no horizon rectangle, no large opaque shadow on the background. Preserve clean anti-aliased cutout edges. Natural landforms may form an irregular boundary.
Simplification is critical: remove the mountains full of contour lines, almost all trees, farms, individual windows, vehicles, ships, tiny people, decorative textures, repeated road networks, multiple cranes and distant settlements. Broad shapes and a handful of focal objects. Fine-detail realism is not the aim. Avoid neon synthwave lighting, robots, spacecraft, logos, watermarks and text.

Edit the supplied colored landscape cutout, preserving its broad composition, natural palette, three building masses, water, bridge and single construction site. Keep the genuinely transparent background.
Two precise corrections for a small printed placement on WHITE paper:
1. The OUTER capability frontier must be much clearer. Replace the nearly invisible fine line hugging the far silhouette with a bold NAVY BLUE DASHED CURVE laid across the broad open upper plateau, about one quarter of the way down from the top, between the upper ridge and central crane. Use a few large, widely spaced dashes comparable in stroke width to the existing inner solid navy frontier. This second boundary must remain visible when the whole image is printed at only 165 mm wide. Keep the inner solid frontier around the near-left settlement.
2. Clean all cutout edges: remove every stray red, yellow, cyan or electric-blue fringe, preserve natural clean antialiased RGBA transparency, with no opaque background rectangle or external shadow. Make the fine surface texture slightly softer so it does not compete with the two frontier lines and the main structures.
No labels, no text, no new buildings, no extra cranes or fine decorative details. Preserve the open, unexplored terrain and all other major elements.
